title: What AI tools do you guys use for UI design?
author: Proof_Head7095
selftext:
I’ve been trying to use ChatGPT for UI design iterations, but I’m honestly not very happy with the results so far. Even when I provide an existing UI and ask it to improve or polish it, the output still feels pretty rough or generic.

Are there any AI tools that are actually good at UI/UX design and understand modern design principles? Curious what workflows or tools you guys use.

replies.author: Useful_Use_6170
replies.body: Didn’t even know that was a thing gonna try it out now! And then how do you get it to work in like godot ? Or base44?

comments.author: PhotojournalistBig53
comments.body: Doing it manually in photoshop tbh. Sure Claude can get some USS-elements in but it doesn’t do a good job with the experience part of it. It’s mostly shapes and text anyways so not like you need a steady hand for it.

comments.author: AdrianRWalker
comments.body: Honestly Chat GPT has give me awesome UI layouts that I then build in Unity.

comments.author: m3tr1c__
comments.body: have you tried using one of the coding models (i.e. codex, claude code), or qre you just using straight chatgpt?

comments.author: Content_Eggplant2018
comments.body: ChatGPT is great for generating ideas and iterating on UI concepts quickly, but it's not a replacement for human judgment and design expertise just yet. Have you considered using tools like Figma's auto-layout feature or Adobe XD's AI-powered UI element suggestions to get started with automation, then still having designers review and refine the output? These can help bridge the gap between creative direction and technical execution.

comments.author: Mysterious_Gold3137
comments.body: Claude Design or Figma Make: Use Figma Make for less refined work, and Claude Design for a more stylized look.

comments.author: Soft-Fly-640
comments.body: If your into mobile UI design, Try [Pixarc](http://www.pixarc.co), it supports native UI code export too.

comments.author: 9udby3tt
comments.body:
if there are, I’d say tools like Replit or Claude are probably closer since they let you add more context and even style guides.

but honestly, I think it still mostly comes down to your own design taste and understanding of good UI first.

AI tools are getting better really fast, but right now I still see them more as support tools to speed up the process, not something that fully replaces UI/UX thinking. what helped me more was spending time exploring great references from sites like awwwards, godly, pinterest, or real live products. 

then when you use AI, you already know what direction you want. AI becomes much more useful when you give it strong references, clear context, and use it for exploration instead of expecting perfect final UI instantly. also, detail prompt saves tokens <:p

for me, the best workflow right now is still: AI for speed, humans for taste and judgment p:

replies.author: Mission_Star_9079
replies.body: but it's a little expensive to me

comments.author: SignatureQuick2001
comments.body: I like cursor for coding over claude code and [klyxx.io](http://klyxx.io) is a great tool for UX/UI screen audits and also fix prompts.
